title: Composite latency scoring for cross-region prioritization and model-variant fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Region selection today is either static affinities or single-metric thresholds (p95). This leads to noisy failovers, oscillation when telemetry is sparse, and suboptimal use of lower-cost tiers or model variants. Goal: Implement a composite region scoring function that combines latency percentiles (p50/p95), network error/packet-loss signal, recent staleness of telemetry, and capacity headroom to produce a single rankable score per region. That score will drive (1) region routing decisions for incoming requests, (2) tier routing (hosted vs dedicated) preference, and (3) ordered fallback model variants when the preferred region cannot meet SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: A configurable composite scoring function exists with weights for p50, p95, packet_loss, telemetry_staleness_penalty, and headroom
Score computation is emitted to metrics pipeline at 30s intervals per region and is queryable from the routing service
Routing decisions based on the composite score reduce p95 tail region-induced latency incidents by at least 20% in synthetic traffic tests compared to baseline p95-only policy
Fallback model variant ordering is respected: runtime prefers same-region compatible quantized variant before cross-region full-precision variant when score within fallback_threshold
Feature flag + canary rollout path available; safe rollback documented
Unit/integration tests and simulation harness validate staleness behavior and weight tuning
implementation_notes: Telemetry inputs: region-level p50, p95 (1m and 5m windows), packet_loss (1m), recent_5m_request_rate, capacity_headroom (GPUs free / total), last_update_timestamp
Scoring formula (configurable): region_score = normalize(p95)*w_p95 + normalize(p50)*w_p50 + packet_loss*w_loss + staleness_penalty*w_stale - headroom_boost*w_headroom
Normalization: dynamically compute historical deciles; fallback to fixed caps for cold-start regions to avoid extreme weights
Staleness handling: if last_update > staleness_threshold (default 120s) apply exponential staleness_penalty; also mark region as 'degraded' when telemetry absent > 300s
Smoothing: use EWMA with alpha configurable per-metric to avoid oscillation; expose alpha through config store
Config: weights and thresholds stored in routing-config service (per-customer overrides supported), persisted in runtime-1.20 release config bundle

Fallback ordering: each model in catalog has variant compatibility table per region (latency-compatible, quantized-supported). Routing uses composite score plus variant affinity to produce candidate list. When top region score degrades below soft_threshold, try quantized variant in same region; when below hard_threshold, route to next-ranked region's primary variant
Circuit breaker: implement rapid failover if successive requests get errors > 5% within 30s despite good score
Telemetry pipeline changes: add score emission metric 'region.composite_score' with tags {region, tier, model_family} and tracing context for sample requests
Backward compatibility: retain existing p95-only policy as a flag and compare A/B metrics in rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Simulation (dev env): implement scoring logic in routing-sim harness, run synthetic traffic across 10 region stubs and validate policy under noise and partial telemetry
Phase 2 - Internal canary (10% traffic): enable composite scoring for internal accounts; collect metrics and compare to baseline for 2 weeks
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp (50% -> 100%): increase traffic by 20% every 48 hours if p95 and error rate stable; keep auto-rollback on threshold breach
Phase 4 - Model-variant fallback enabled: enable ordered fallback per config and validate through chaos tests that quantized fallbacks maintain latency/cost targets
Rollback: flip feature flag and allow warmup period of 60s for prior routing to settle; run postmortem if rollback occurs
metrics: p50/p95 per-region per-tier (existing) for pre/post comparison
fallback.invocations counter with labels fallback_type (quantized_same_region, full_precision_cross_region)
routing.latency.delta (time to decision) — must be < 5ms additional compared to baseline
dependencies: ENG-27410 (telemetry-aggregation-pipeline): ensure packet_loss and headroom metrics available
INFRA-112 (config-store TLS rotation): runtime needs access to routing config
